title: Add proof logger interface
body:
Work towards a `--proof-log` option which is working on this branch: https://github.com/ajreynol/CVC4/tree/proofLog

This class will be overridden by a CPC proof logger initially.

title: Disable checking options in subsolvers used by quantifiers modules
body: This should be done regardless but is necessary for a new proof logging infrastructure, where we do not want to log proofs in subsolvers.

title: More fixes for proof configuration in `pp-only` mode
body:
Note this now allows full proofs to be returned when `proof-mode=pp-only`.

This also means that proofs are available when unsat cores are enabled (although they will contain a single trusted SAT_REFUTATION the SAT portion by default).

Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-projects/issues/743.

Further fixes a potential configuration option where unsat cores would mistakenly be based on SAT proofs if the proof mode was explicitly set to `pp-only`.

title: [proofs] [alethe] Update doc, remove experimental option
Fix a few options classification
body: These options shouldn't impact the behavior of the solver in any significant way, moreover we need them to be common for use in combination with `--safe-options`.

title: Minor fix for MBQI, add regressions for fixed issues
body:
Two issues were fixed by dropping an experimental sets option, the 3rd is fixed by not allowing certain kinds of terms to appear in MBQI reasoning.

Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-projects/issues/733.
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-projects/issues/731.
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-projects/issues/728.

title: Use smt2 printer for skolems when printing cpc proofs
body:
This updates the cpc printer to use the native option for printing skolems (--print-skolem-definitions). This avoids spurious node conversion.

Several changes were necessary:
- The smt2 printer for skolems now threads a let binding utility, since skolem indices can be letified. Furthermore a bug in this method is fixed.
- The let bind utility was extended to optionally traverse skolems (off by default).
- The cpc printer no longer converts handled skolems, unless their indices change.
- The skolem manager is simplified to not automatically sort indices, instead this is lifted to the API level. (Otherwise this would flip indices unsoundly during node conversion).
- The Ethos version is updated to one where a bug in `:opaque` is fixed.

title: cmake: Check whether CoCoA has been patched
body:
If CoCoA has not been patched and the `--auto-download` option is provided, CMake will build a patched version for the user.

Resolves #11182

title: Disable support for experimental theories when safe-options is set
body:
This adds options that guard the usage of "experimental" theories or extensions thereof when `--safe-options` is enabled.

This includes bags, finite fields, separation logic, higher-order logic, and extensions of arithmetic (including transcendentals, iand and pow2).

The options `--sets-exp` (renamed from `--sets-ext` in this PR) and `--fp-exp` continue to be disabled by default, thus do not need to change.

Similar to other expert options, these theories can still be used with `safe-options` if they are enabled prior to setting `safe-options`, e.g. `--ho-exp --safe-options ...` allows HOL to be used.  The options configuration will only override the setting of `*-exp` options if not set by user.

This does not impact the behavior of cvc5 when `--safe-options` is not set.

FYI @alex-ozdemir @mudathirmahgoub @yoni206 .

title: Add option to print uninterpreted sorts as a datatype in models
Remove option `strings-code-elim`
body: Makes `seq.nth` only apply to sequences.  Deletes a now irrelevant RARE rewrite.

title: Add more improvements to rewrite proof construction
body:
Makes the following improvements:
- A buffer is used to make the recursion in the class a bit more clear and eliminates the need for some temporary variables.
- A new tactic CONG_FLATTEN is used which is helpful when proving rewrites where a trivial flattening step is necessary. For example 
`(= (str.len (str.++ x y z "A" w)) (+ (str.len x) (str.len y) (str.len z) 1 (str.len w))`, 
where the fixed point rule proves
`(= (str.len (str.++ x y z "A" w)) (+ (str.len x) (+ (str.len y) (+ (str.len z) (+ (str.len "A") (str.len w))))))`
The cong flatten tactic recognizes that the two RHS align and thus we try to prove the components equal.
- The step limit is increased as it helps in practice.
- Stratification of the search is optional, mostly as a way of debugging.

title: Enable term-db-mode=relevant by default
body:
This option makes it so that only terms that appear in assertions are considered e.g. for E-matching.  This is in contrast to the default behavior where additionally "preregistered" terms are considered.

This gives convincing results on SMT-LIB quantified logics:
+293-167 over 86550 benchmarks in logics with UF and quantifiers.
it is 9.7% faster on average on commonly solved instances 16820s vs 18467s.

title: Add conflict processor option
body: Adds expert option to enable the module introduced in https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/10738.

title: Restrict the combination of let terms and variable shadowing
body:
This reenables non-fresh binder semantics by default (i.e. `--fresh-binders` is `false`), as introduced in https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/10556 and disabled in https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/11076.

The motivation for this change is that ALF proofs involving quantifiers are incorrect on main, and distributed solving is expected to suffer major performance issues unless `--fresh-binders` is false.  This PR is a medium term solution until we either support object syntax for let (e.g. a `Kind::LET`) or refactor how these features are handled.

We now restrict the combination of variable shadowing and `let` within quantified formula bodies to avoid potential for unsoundness.

This means that we are *not* SMT-LIB compliant in that we reject corner cases like the one mentioned on #11066.  This is the only case of this combination in all of our regressions, which includes rerunning all regressions through the `dump` tester (there are 9 cases where `let` and variable shadowing are used in a benign way).

The user can always use `--fresh-binders` if they wish for cvc5 to be SMT-LIB compliant, but this option is incompatible with proofs.

Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-wishues/issues/152.

title: Revert to fresh binder semantics in parser
body:
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/issues/11066.

This reverts a change to how variables are parsed as introduced in https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/10556.

After this PR, the reverted behavior is available with `--no-fresh-binders`, but still suffers from potential unsoundness demonstrated on https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/issues/11066.

In particular, with non-fresh binders, it is possible to use SMT-LIB `let` to generate a term that is not properly interpreted by our parser, as demonstrated by the minimal example on that issue. In particular, since we do not interpret `let` as object syntax, the minimized benchmark on that issue leads to a substitution that is not capture avoiding.

The option `--no-fresh-binders` should be considered moving forward for proofs / distributed solving but will need a workaround to address the above issue, either by making `let` object syntax or further restricting which inputs we allow in the parser.

title: Retire competition scripts from 2024 and remove usage of --arrays-weak-equiv
body:
This pull request creates a copy of the competition scripts to document the state of the scripts as they were used for the 2024 competition.

It also removes all uses of the experimental option `--arrays-weak-equiv`.  This is done in two commits. The first commit removes it from the single query script, and the second commit removes it from the unsat-cores script after the 2024 copies are created.
The problem with `--arrays-weak-equiv` is documented here.

title: String Reversal Simplification
body:
**Describe the bug**
Not a bug, but a place for performance improvement in the string solver. The following test takes a long time to be solved despite being quite simple: 
[symcc-structs-assertions-modified.smt2.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16110870/symcc-structs-assertions-modified.smt2.txt)

Below is a description of the test.
This test contains three assertions.
1. The length of the input string, stdin0, is asserted to be 4.
2. stdin0 is reversed (_let_2) and reversed again (_let_3), so that \_let\_3 should be the original string. When each byte of stdin0 is converted to a bitvector and concated together, then the result should be less than (\_ bv17 32).
3. stdin0 is fully reversed as above, twice in this assertion. \_let\_5 should be the original string. Again, when the string is converted to a bitvector again as above, the result should be greater than (\_ bv3 32).

This test takes about a minute to be solved on my local machine (both with commit 4c9e41618757cdf8fcea8c97a1d2a4221bbdf484 and with PR#10717). However, when I make the number of string reversals the same in both assertions (either one full reversal as in the second assertion, or two full reversals as in the third assertion), then this test takes less than a second. It seems like the solver is not recognizing that a finite-length string that is reversed twice is the same as the original, something that I believe is always true (unless there is are some tricky details I'm missing!).

title: Incompleteness with experimental option --arrays-weak-equiv
body:
**Describe the bug**

The following problem is unsatisfiable, but cvc5 returns `sat` when the experimental option `--arrays-weak-equiv` is used.

```scheme
(set-logic QF_ABV)
(declare-const a1 (Array (_ BitVec 1) (_ BitVec 1)))
(declare-const a2 (Array (_ BitVec 1) (_ BitVec 1)))
(declare-const i (_ BitVec 1))
(assert (= #b0 (select a2 #b0)))
(assert (= #b1 (select a2 i)))
(assert (= (store a2 #b0 #b1) (store (store a1 #b0 #b1) #b1 #b0)))
(assert (not (= a2 (store a2 #b0 #b1))))
(check-sat)
```

**Command line arguments**: `--arrays-weak-equiv`
**cvc5 version/commit**: 15fbdbd04588bf54d10a46e6d09d6a7a8507d566

### Notes

The method implemented by this option is described here: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.6939

The last assert (starting with `(not (=`) is superfluous, but removing it makes the bug disappear.

Determining the unsatisfiability of the problem requires reasoning about `i`: it can't be `0` because of the first `assert`, it can't be `1` because of the third assert, and it can't take any other value, because it's a bitvector of length `1`.

Tracing using `-t arrays -t arrays-merge -t arrays-lem -t pf::array --no-arrays-optimize-linear` indicates that the the arrays solver with weak-equiv generates one lemma.

Both versions of the array solver introduce a skolem `@array_deq_diff_1` that stands for the evidence
for the `not (=` in the last assert.  Hence, this skolem is defined with
```scheme
(or         (=         a2                            (store a2 #b0 #b1)) 
       (not (= (select a2 @array_deq_diff_1) (select (store a2 #b0 #b1) @array_deq_diff_1))))
```

Throughout the entire run the array solver with weak-equiv generates only one lemma.  This lemma expresses
that `@array_deq_diff_1` must be =`#b0`:
```scheme
(or (= (select a2 @array_deq_diff_1) (select (store a2 #b0 #b1) @array_deq_diff_1))
    (= @array_deq_diff_1 #b0))
```

This is clearly not enough, because we need to say something about `i`. The array solver without weak equivalences produces such lemmas.
For example, it produces
```scheme
(or (= i #b0) (= (select a2 i) (select (store a2 #b0 #b1) i)))
```

The weak-equivalences lemmas are generated here: https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/blob/main/src/theory/arrays/theory_arrays.cpp#L1280

The problem induces the weak equivalence
```
a2 <- #b0 -> (store a2 #b0 #b1) <-->  (store (store a1 #b0 #b1) #b1 #b0)
```
Now in an arrangement where `i` is equivalent to `1` we would get the `read-over-weakeq` lemma:
```
(not (= i 1)) ∨ (= i 0) ∨ (not (= (store a2 #b0 #b1) (store (store a1 #b0 #b1) #b1 #b0))) ∨
(= (select a2 #b1) (select (store (store a1 #b0 #b1) #b1 #b0)) #b1)
```
which directly leads to unsat.
However, when I print the equivalence classes when the lemmas are generated, `i` is alone. Hence, this lemma cannot be generated.

### Weak Equivalences and Bitvector Indices

There is some lingering doubt whether we can reliably use this method when the array index is a theory that is not stable infinite (such as bitvectors).
The paper states in the related work section:
> We [..] add some requirements on the index theory that prevent the procedure presented in this paper from using the theory of bitvectors as index theory.

However, section 6 gives the impression that this might just be because of an **optimization**.  They says you can omit the creation of certain `select` terms for stably infinite theories (if I understand the code correctly we introduce those `select` terms in any case.) 

However, the soundness proof of the **un**optimized version uses index theories with infinite models:
> we assume every sort σ that is used as index sort for an array sort contains an infinite supply of fresh domain elements

This might also be affected by how cvc5 does theory combination.

### Smaller Benchmark

An even smaller problem that exhibits the same bug is:
```scheme
(set-logic ALL)
(declare-const a (Array (_ BitVec 1) (_ BitVec 1)))
(declare-const b (Array (_ BitVec 1) (_ BitVec 1)))
(declare-const i (_ BitVec 1))
(assert (= #b1 (select a i)))
(assert (= (store a #b0 #b1) (store b #b1 #b0)))
(assert (not (= a (store a #b0 #b1))))
(check-sat)
```

title: Add suggestions for how to avoid option exception with `--safe-options`
Add `--uf-lambda-qe` to eagerly eliminate quantifiers in HO lambda equivalence
body:
This adds an option to eagerly eliminate quantified formulas when two lambdas are equated.

For example, say `(= f1 f2)` where `f1` is `(lambda ((x Int)) (< x a))` and `f2` is `(lambda ((x Int)) (< x b))`.

By default, we would generate the inference `(=> (= f1 f2) (forall ((x Int)) (= (< x a) (< x b)))`, where quantified reasoning is introduced into the main solving procedure.

With `--uf-lambda-qe`, we use a subsolver to compute the quantifier elimination of `(forall ((x Int)) (= (< x a) (< x b))`, which is `(and (<= a b) (<= b a))`. We instead generate the lemma `(=> (= f1 f2) (and (<= a b) (<= b a))`.

The motivation for this is to reduce the complexity of constraints in the main solver. This is motivated by usages of `set.filter` where the lambdas are over a decidable theory that admits quantifier elimination, e.g. `LIA` or `BV`.

title: Add portfolio config option
body: This also adds the new config option as a requirement for the portfolio-out.smt2 test so that it is skipped on Windows.

title: Implement printing for skolems
body:
This PR adds an option `--print-skolem-definitions` (disabled by default) to print skolems based on their formal definitions.

This will eventually be used when exporting terms via the text interface.

It also makes a minor modification to `QUANTIFIERS_SKOLEMIZE` to take the variable instead of the index, as this corrects a special case in the ALF proof signature. FYI @HanielB 

Furthermore skolem names are now lowercase (prefixed by `@`) for consistency with other operators.

title: cvc5 replies "unsupported" for SMTLIB standard option `random-seed`, but accepts nonstandard option `seed`
body:
**Describe the bug**

```
cvc5> (set-option :print-success true)
success
cvc5> (set-option :random-seed 42)
unsupported
cvc5> (set-option :seed 42)
success
```

cvc5 ought to support the standard option.

title: String Simplification
body:
[str20.smt2.txt](https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/files/14657704/str20.smt2.txt)

**Describe the bug**
This file is not being simplified to the degree I would expect (these are the dumped assertions after calling simplify in the C++ API -- simplify did not change any of the original assertions). The length of stdin0 is known to be 4 (first assertion), so I would expect for example (str.len (str.substr stdin 0 1)) to simplify to 1, but this is not being done. When I manually simplify the file, CVC5 returns unsat immediately, but when I run the original file, it does not terminate in any reasonable amount of time.

  --ipo                    build with interprocedural optimization

Optional Packages:
The following flags enable optional packages (disable with --no-<option name>).

  --cryptominisat          use the CryptoMiniSat SAT solver
  --kissat                 use the Kissat SAT solver

  exit 0
}

}

}

[ ! -e src/theory ] && die "$0 not called from CVC4 base directory"

build_dir=build
install_prefix=default

asan=default

if command -v python3 &> /dev/null; then

do

body:
**Describe the bug**
The SMT-LIB 2.5 standard introduced `check-sat-assuming` and `get-unsat-assumptions`. However, Cvc5 (default configuration) produces an error unless you set the Cvc5 specific solver flag `--incremental`. This makes it seem like the default cvc5 configuration isn't quite SMT-LIB 2.5/2.6 compliant. 

Here is an example:

```
❯ cat ex.smt2
(set-option :produce-models true)
(set-option :produce-unsat-assumptions true)
(declare-const x Bool)
(declare-const y Bool)
(assert (and x (not y)))
(check-sat-assuming (y))
(get-unsat-assumptions)

❯ cvc5-1.1.1 < ex.smt2
unsat
(error "Cannot get unsat assumptions unless incremental solving is enabled (try --incremental)")
```

I can set `--incremental` or `(set-option :incremental true)` (which doesn't seem to be standard), but it would be nice if this were inferred from `set-option :produce-unsat-assumptions true`.

For comparison, here are z3-4.12.1 and bitwuzla-0.3.0:

```
❯ bitwuzla-0.3.0 < ex.smt2
unsat
(y)

❯ z3-4.12.1 < ex.smt2
unsat
(y)

title: Set Product and Folding in C++
Global declarations behavior differs when piping from stdin vs a file
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reading SMT2 commands from stdin appears to set the global-declarations option to true unconditionally, while reading from a file properly respects the options. It works "differently" in cvc5 v1.0.4 and doesn't work with cvc5 1.1.0; not sure about other versions.

Example file (push-pop.smt):
```smt
(set-logic ALL)
(push 1)
(declare-const z Int)
(pop 1)
(push 1)
(declare-const z Int)
(pop 1)
```

v1.0.4 apparently ignores the flag and sets global declarations to off:
```
PS D:\bin> Get-Content .\push-pop.smt | .\cvc5-1.0.4.exe --lang smt2 --incremental
; No error (expected)
PS D:\bin> Get-Content .\push-pop.smt | .\cvc5-1.0.4.exe --lang smt2 --incremental --global-declarations
; No error (not expected?)
```

v1.1.0 apparently ignores the flag and sets global declarations to on:
```
PS D:\bin> Get-Content .\push-pop.smt | .\cvc5-1.1.0.exe --lang smt2 --incremental
(error "Cannot bind z to symbol of type Int, maybe the symbol has already been defined?")   ; <-- Error (not expected)
PS D:\bin> Get-Content .\push-pop.smt | .\cvc5-1.1.0.exe --lang smt2 --incremental --no-global-declarations
(error "Cannot bind z to symbol of type Int, maybe the symbol has already been defined?")   ; <-- Error (not expected)
```

However, v1.1.0 works as expected when reading directly from a file:
```
PS D:\bin> .\cvc5-1.1.0.exe --lang smt2 --incremental .\push-pop.smt
; No error (expected)
PS D:\bin> .\cvc5-1.1.0.exe --lang smt2 --incremental --global-declarations .\push-pop.smt
(error "Cannot bind z to symbol of type Int, maybe the symbol has already been defined?")   ; <-- Error (expected)
PS D:\bin> .\cvc5-1.1.0.exe --lang smt2 --incremental --no-global-declarations .\push-pop.smt
; No error (expected)
```

**Command line arguments**: `--lang smt2 --incremental`  
**cvc5 version/commit**: v1.1.0 (from GitHub)
**Operating system**: Windows 10 22H2

title: After (set-option :print-success true), cvc5 prints success for echo commands after echoing
body:
Given the following echo.smt2
```
(set-option :print-success true)
(echo "asdf")
```
running `cvc5 echo.smt2` prints:
```
success
"asdf"
success
```
I claim the second `success` should not be printed after the echo response.  The [SMT-LIB standard v2.6-r2021-05-12](https://smtlib.cs.uiowa.edu/papers/smt-lib-reference-v2.6-r2021-05-12.pdf) section 4.1.2 says (emphasis mine)

> The value success is the default response for a successful execution of a supported command. A number of commands have a more detailed response **in place of** success, discussed in Section 4.2 for each of them.

and `echo` is one such command.  The definition of `<general_response>` shown in 4.1.2 gives `<specific_success_response>` as an alternative to (i.e., not combined with) `success`.  At the end of appendix B, `<echo_response>` is one of the alternatives presented for `<specific_success_response>`.

I'm working with a Python script that drives either z3 or cvc5 as a subprocess.  In normal operation my script uses `echo` after blocks of commands to synchronize with the solver, but for debugging, my script additionally turns on print-success and flushes after every command so I can associate errors with single commands.  z3 does not print success after echoing, and cvc5 does.  My script expects z3's behavior and gets out of sync with cvc5, which made debugging my own bug very confusing.

I suspect fixing this will break someone else's code that (perhaps accidentally) depends on the current behavior, so it may be better to just document it, though it's not clear where.  (z3 requires `(set-option :smtlib2_compliant true)` to (among other things) print the quotes around the echoed string, but cvc5 doesn't seem to have a similar standards-compliance option.)

**Command line arguments**: no arguments passed

title: Compilation error in make check for  node_traversal_black.cpp
body:
**Describe the bug**

When compiling cvc5 in debug mode and running `make check`, I see a compiler error related to
instantiating the `std::copy` template.

This happens with clang 15.0.0 on my Mac (running Mac OSX Ventura 13.6.1), but I don't think it's compiler
related. It's caused by the definition of the `std::copy` template in the LLVM libcxx:
(see https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/libcxx/include/__algorithm/copy.h)

Here's the compiler error.

```
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX14.2.sdk/usr/include/c++/v1/__utility/pair.h:74:5: error: the parameter for this explicitly-defaulted copy constructor is const, but a member or base requires it to be non-const
    pair(pair const&) = default;
    ^
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX14.2.sdk/usr/include/c++/v1/__algorithm/copy.h:111:1: note: in instantiation of template class 'std::pair<cvc5::internal::NodeDfsIterator, std::back_insert_iterator<std::vector<cvc5::internal::NodeTemplate<false>>>>' requested here
__copy(_InIter __first, _Sent __last, _OutIter __result) {
^
/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX14.2.sdk/usr/include/c++/v1/__algorithm/copy.h:119:15: note: in instantiation of function template specialization 'std::__copy<std::_ClassicAlgPolicy, cvc5::internal::NodeDfsIterator, cvc5::internal::NodeDfsIterator, std::back_insert_iterator<std::vector<cvc5::internal::NodeTemplate<false>>>>' requested here
  return std::__copy<_ClassicAlgPolicy>(__first, __last, __result).second;
              ^
/Users/dutebrun/Repos/cvc5/test/unit/node/node_traversal_black.cpp:147:8: note: in instantiation of function template specialization 'std::copy<cvc5::internal::NodeDfsIterator, std::back_insert_iterator<std::vector<cvc5::internal::NodeTemplate<false>>>>' requested here
  std::copy(traversal.begin(), traversal.end(), std::back_inserter(actual));
       ^
1 error generated.

```

**Configure Options**

Here are the steps to reproduce this:
```
./configure.sh debug --auto-download --static
cd build
make
make check
```

The only fix I've found is to replace all the `std::copy` lines with explicit loops in `node_traversal_black.cpp`:
```
  std::vector<TNode> actual;
  for (auto node: traversal) {
    actual.push_back(node);
  }
```

title: Fatal failure within void cvc5::internal::theory::datatypes::SygusExtension::check() at sygus_extension.cpp:1605
body:
**Describe the bug**
Assertion error on using `getAbduct` with a pre-defined grammar. This seems to be happen when I introduce the `And` term below to allow for conjunctions in my grammar along with the `const_2` being able to take any constant.

Test case (using python API):

```python
import cvc5
from cvc5 import *


s = cvc5.Solver()
s.setOption('produce-abducts', 'true')
s.setOption('incremental', 'false')
s.setLogic('QF_BV')

bitvec = s.mkBitVectorSort(2)
boolean = s.getBooleanSort()

x_0_L = s.mkConst(bitvec, 'x_0_L')
x_1_L = s.mkConst(bitvec, 'x_1_L')

const_2 = s.mkVar(bitvec, 'const_2')
start = s.mkVar(boolean, 'start')
eq = s.mkVar(boolean, 'eq')

Eq_x_0 = s.mkTerm(Kind.EQUAL, x_0_L, const_2)
Eq_x_1 = s.mkTerm(Kind.EQUAL, x_1_L, const_2)
And = s.mkTerm(Kind.AND, start, start)

g = s.mkGrammar([], [start, eq, const_2])

g.addAnyConstant(const_2)
g.addRules(start, [And, eq])
g.addRules(eq, [Eq_x_0, Eq_x_1])

print(g)

r = s.mkTerm(Kind.BITVECTOR_OR, x_0_L, x_1_L)

abd = s.getAbduct(s.mkTerm(Kind.EQUAL, r, s.mkBitVector(2, 0)), g)
print(abd)
```

**cvc5 version/commit**: 1.0.8 
**Operating system**: Ubuntu 18.04

title: Add `--pythonic-path=PATH` configuration option.
body:
Now, you can run configuration like this `./configure.sh debug --python-bindings --pythonic-path=PATH --auto-download`.

I've tested it locally.

How should I document it? And/or test it in CI? Not sure if the latter is feasible.

title: Add `--safe-options`
body:
This option indicates that further options cannot be expert.

Note that `--safe-options --expert-option` throws an exception  while `--expert-option --safe-options` does not.

title: Refactor pattern selection utility
body:
Makes it so that options can be provided manually.

Also avoids a tree traversal in `isUsable` and corrects a case where relational triggers could be selected when they are disabled.

title: Refactor and update the RARE parser
body:
A few changes were made to the RARE parser on `proof-new` (see `src/rewriter/README.md`). This PR brings these changes into `main`.
1. The obsolete `let` and `cond` constructions are removed
2. `define-cond-rule*`, which has misleading semantics and is unused, is removed
3. `(define ...)` is added as a possible optional argument to `(define-rule ...)` to define shortcuts
4. Refactors the code for clarity
The operators `INT_ISPOW2` and `INT_LENGTH` are omitted because they don't exist on `main`.

title: `(set-option :dump-unsat-cores-full true)` not working
body:
**Describe the bug**

When following the [Quickstart Guide](https://cvc5.github.io/docs/cvc5-1.0.8/binary/quickstart.html), it is suggested to use `(set-option :dump-unsat-cores-full true)` to include assertions in the unsat core that have not been named.

This does not seem to be working. Instead, cvc5 prints `unsupported` and the requested unsat core returns an empty list.

Minimal example:
```smt
(set-logic ALL)
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)
(set-option :dump-unsat-cores-full true)
(declare-const a Int)
(assert (< 0 a))
(assert (> 0 a))
(check-sat)
(get-unsat-core)
```

cvc5 output:
```smt
unsupported
unsat
(
)
```

**Operating system**: NixOS 23.05

Also removes an experimental proof rule file (Conversions.smt3) which was added by mistake.

title: Formula describing Euclidean algorithm (gcd) does not finish
body:
**Describe the bug**
I encountered a fairly small and simple example that does not get solved within 1 hour.
I expect this example to be very easy and fast to solve.

```smt
(set-logic NIA)
(declare-const a0 Int)
(declare-const b0 Int)
(declare-const a1 Int)
(declare-const b1 Int)
(declare-const a2 Int)
(declare-const b2 Int)
(declare-const a3 Int)
(declare-const b3 Int)
(assert (and
	(= a0 12)
	(= b0 9)
	(exists ((q Int)) (and (>= b1 0) (< b1 b0) (= (+ (* b0 q) b1) a0)))
	(= a1 b0)
	(exists ((q Int)) (and (>= b2 0) (< b2 b1) (= (+ (* b1 q) b2) a1)))
	(= a2 b1)
	; remove the next two lines to have an example that is solved very fast
	(exists ((q Int)) (and (>= b3 0) (< b3 b2) (= (+ (* b2 q) b3) a2)))
	(= a3 b2)
))
(check-sat)
```
```
$ time ./cvc5 slow.smt2
^Ccvc5 interrupted by user.

./cvc5 slow.smt2  5197.79s user 0.92s system 99% cpu 1:26:47.64 total
```
It was my first time using `ddSMT` and after seeing no progress for 5 minutes I decided to skip it.

**Context of the formula**
In case that might help, I will explain the formula.
This models the computation of the greatest common divisor using the [Euclidean algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_common_divisor#Euclid's_algorithm).
The algorithm replaces `(a, b)` by `(b, a mod b)` repeatedly until the pair is `(d, 0)`, where d is the greatest common divisor.
The modulo operation is modeled by existentially quantifying the quotient. (Expert opinion welcome: is there a better way to model the modulo operation?)
Each quantified term corresponds to a step in the algorithm.
With the first two iterations we find that `gcd(12,9) = gcd(9,3) = gcd(3,0) = 3`.
So we know that `a2 = 3` and `b2 = 0`.
Inserting into `(exists ((q Int)) (and (>= b3 0) (< b3 b2) (= (+ (* b2 q) b3) a2)))`,
we can clearly see that `b3 >= 0` and `b3 < 0`. A contradiction independent of q, so the entire term is unsat.
For some other starting values a0 and b0 the solver finishes immediately.

**Command line arguments**: none
**cvc5 version/commit**: Latest release download from GitHub
**Operating system**: Arch Linux 

**`configure.sh` options**  
Not applicable / whatever was used for the release.

**`configure.sh` output**  
Not applicable / whatever was used for the release.

title: Make int-blasting a regular option
body:
Int-blasting was experimental, and this PR makes it a regular option.
Notice that still there are some features of int-blasting that remain experimental (e.g. granularity). 
We plan to move them to the regular options in the sequel.
Relates to #10084 .

title: Java memory leak
body:
**Describe the bug**
I use the Java bindings to create a lot of solvers. It appears that some of that memory is not released. The process eats up all available memory on the system until the OS freezes and I have to reboot.

I made a small example program to reproduce the issue. The heap memory does not exceed 16 MB, But the Process uses all available 14 GB. Be aware, that **executing this example freezes my PC within about 30 seconds**, forcing me to reboot. I suggest to take precautions like running in a VM maybe, to avoid the pain.

```java
public class Leak {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    while (true) {
      Solver solver = new Solver();
      Term x = solver.mkConst(solver.getIntegerSort());
      Term y = solver.mkConst(solver.getIntegerSort());
      Term two = solver.mkInteger(2);
      // x = 2 AND y = 2*x
      Term assertion = x.eqTerm(two).andTerm(y.eqTerm(solver.mkTerm(Kind.MULT, x, two)));
      solver.assertFormula(assertion);
      Result result = solver.checkSat();
      if (!result.isSat()) {
        System.exit(1);
      }
      //solver.deletePointer();
    }
  }
}
```

If the last line `solver.deletePointer()` is present, the memory leak persists, although it takes a lot longer to fill my ram. In my real application it is not sufficient to include that line; presumably because the terms are much larger.

Manually dropping all pointers from Java code is not a task I would trust Java developers with. We're not trained in manual memory management and would mess this up. Manually releasing just the solver is however feasible. The idiomatic pattern for that would be to add `Solver implements AutoClosable`. That would make the compiler warn about forgetting to close the solver and enable the try-with-resource syntax. 

On a related note: There is a good chance I should not be creating this many solvers. But I think I need to, because I use a breadth first search algorithm that has to check very long formulas in each node. The formula for checking if a node should be expanded is the conjunction of all predecessor nodes plus some extra. I feel like I the solver might be able to take advantage of reusing all that work. But since it has to be a breadth first search, that would eat all my memory even without a leak.

title: Inconsistent printing for quoted identifiers
body:
Quoted identifiers are sometimes printed without `|` from a `get-value` call.

**Command line arguments**: `-L smtlib`
**cvc5 version/commit**: 
This is cvc5 version 1.0.6 [git tag 1.0.6 branch HEAD]
compiled with GCC version Apple LLVM 14.0.0 (clang-1400.0.29.202)

**Operating system**: Mac OS

For the following input file:
```racket
(set-option :produce-models true)
(declare-fun |Aparam0| () Int)
(declare-fun |Eparam1| () Int)
(declare-fun |BZ0::Eparam2| () Int)
(declare-fun |BZ1::Eparam3| () Int)
(declare-fun |'Gevent0| () Int)
(define-fun e2 () Int |Aparam0|)
(define-fun e3 () Int |Eparam1|)
(define-fun e4 () Int |BZ0::Eparam2|)
(define-fun e5 () Int |BZ1::Eparam3|)
(define-fun e6 () Int (+ e4 e5))
(define-fun prop0 () Bool false)
(define-fun prop1 () Bool true)
(define-fun prop2 () Bool (> e3 e2))
(define-fun prop3 () Bool (> e4 e2))
(define-fun prop4 () Bool (> e5 e2))
(define-fun prop5 () Bool (= e3 e6))
(define-fun prop6 () Bool (and prop3 prop5))
(define-fun prop7 () Bool (and prop4 prop6))
(define-fun prop8 () Bool (=> prop7 prop2))
(assert (not prop8))
(check-sat)
(get-value (|Eparam1|))
```

When running with Z3, we get:
```
% z3 -smt2 model.smt      
sat
((|Eparam1| (- 2)))
```

When running cvc5:
```
% cvc5 model.smt -L smtlib
model.smt:2.2: No set-logic command was given before this point.
model.smt:2.2: cvc5 will make all theories available.
model.smt:2.2: Consider setting a stricter logic for (likely) better performance.
model.smt:2.2: To suppress this warning in the future use (set-logic ALL).
sat
((Eparam1 (- 2)))
```

Note that the cvc5 output is missing the `|` around `Eparam1`.

title: Fixes for strings normal forms and irrelevant terms
body:
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-projects/issues/647.

In particular, we were previously computing normal forms for irrelevant terms (those not appearing in currently asserted literals), which could lead to an incorrect order in which normal forms were processed.

In the PR, we also no longer consider string eq classes containing only irrelevant terms.

Note that due to our eager preregistration policy, string terms are all relevant unless experimental option `strings-eager-reg` is set to false.

title: options: Store option category in internal options info.
options: bv: Rename SatSolverMode to BvSatSolverMode.
Add optional fresh argument to declareFun
body:
This allows the user to have a consistent way of constructing constants (when fresh=false), without manually tracking a symbol table.

It also adds an option `fresh-declarations` to control whether the parser uses fresh constants.  This is true by default to preserve backwards compatibility.

It also fixes an issue with using global-declarations from CLI.

title: c api: First draft of new C API.
body:
This is a first draft of the new C API. The C API will be built on top of the C++ API.

This is a large file (sorry about that), but it makes sense to see it as a whole for review.

**Note:**
* This does not include anything related to `class DriverOptions`.
* This does not yet allow explicit garbage collection atm. That is, once a term/sort or other object is created, there's no way to explicitly release it. I suggest to add this feature later on when the C API is fully implemented and stable.
* Currently, creation of terms and sorts is **tied to a solver instance** on the C++ level. This already decouples term and sort creation from the solver and associates it with a `Cvc5TermManager` as a first step towards **disentangling** this. We will introduce a C++ API-level TermManager (and refactor NodeManager to not be a thread local singleton) to avoid problems with multi-threaded garbage collection (such as in Ocaml) at a later point.

title: Datatype declarations not handled correctly in print_benchmarks.cpp
body:
The `printAssertions` code in `smt/print_benchmarks.cpp` has several issues related to datatypes.

1) If a datatype is parametric, `printAssertions` will print the datatype definition multiple
times (once for the datatype itself + once for every instance). It will also incorrectly
print a `(declare-sort ..)` for the type parameters.

   Example:
   ```
   (set-logic ALL)
   (declare-sort S 0)
   (declare-datatype Option (par (X) ( (none) (some (val X)))))
   (declare-const x (Option S))
   (declare-const y (Option S))
   (assert (= x y))
   (check-sat)
   (exit)
   ```
   Then `cvc5 --output=pre-asserts` prints:
   ```
   ;; pre-asserts start
   (set-logic ALL)
   (declare-sort X 0)
   (declare-datatypes ((Option 1)) ((par (X)((none) (some (val X)))))).
   (declare-sort S 0)
   (declare-datatypes ((Option 1)) ((par (X)((none) (some (val X))))))

title: Print benchmark code does not handle uninterpreted sort constructors

(declare-sort T 0)

(declare-fun y () (S T))

(check-sat)

sat

(declare-const x (S (Option Int)))

title: Refactor expression miner interface
body:
This is work towards a major refactor of our algorithms for expression mining (rewrite rule synthesis and verification, query generation).  The plan is to make these available via a `find-synth` command, see the changes in the regressions for examples.  Currently, these algorithms are available via options that "hijack" calls to `check-sat`/`check-synth`, which is highly non-intuitive and requires modifications to the core of the SyGuS solver.

This changes the interface to expression miner in preparation for this change.

Note this currently removes our support for expression mining via options (which is marked as expert options only).  Support for these will be available again when support for `find-synth` is completed.  Several regressions are disabled in the meantime.

title: Minor improvements to Sygus `rcons` procedure.
body:
This PR adds minor improvements to the SyGuS solver:
- Changes the weight of identity rules in the grammar, giving them higher priority during enumeration.
- Replaces n-ary operators with their binary version before matching in rcons.
- Splits the pattern enumerator for rcons into two enumerators: pattern enumerator and term enumerator.
- Adds an option to control geometric distribution parameter used to interleave the 2 enumerators.

Additionally, this PR moves the implementation of the grammar API to an internal class with the `Grammar` class now a wrapper for the internal class.

title: Removed -j option from command that builds tests.
body: The parallel option `-j` does not seem to be accepted by cmake in some situations. This PR removes this option from commands that build tests. These commands were part of a recent workaround to have 'make test' work (#9750).

title: CMake configure fails with Python >= 3.11
body:
**Describe the bug**

When running the ./configure.sh script, it fails when a newer (>= 3.11) version of Python is installed.  See the output below.  Any Python >= 3.11 is rejected by CMake.  Python 3.11 is the default on the latest Fedora version 38.  After extending the Python versions in `cmake/Helpers.cmake` all works.  The simple bug fix is as follows:

```
diff --git a/cmake/Helpers.cmake b/cmake/Helpers.cmake
index a90f94622..55f514cd4 100644
--- a/cmake/Helpers.cmake
+++ b/cmake/Helpers.cmake
@@ -258,11 +258,11 @@ endfunction()
 
 macro(find_supported_python_version)
   if(${CMAKE_VERSION} VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL "3.19")
-    find_package(Python 3.6...<3.10.999 COMPONENTS Interpreter REQUIRED)
+    find_package(Python 3.6...<3.11.999 COMPONENTS Interpreter REQUIRED)
   else()
     # The version range syntax is only supported from CMake 3.19 on.
     # So, for previous versions, we manually search for an allowed python version
-    foreach (python_version 3.10 3.9 3.8 3.7 3.6)
+    foreach (python_version 3.11 3.10 3.9 3.8 3.7 3.6)
       find_package(Python ${python_version} EXACT COMPONENTS Interpreter)
       if(${Python_FOUND})
         break()
```

**Command line arguments**: N/A
**cvc5 version/commit**:  024777bc78b45ad5852715403af035b0dc615e62
**Operating system**: Linux/Fedora 38

**`configure.sh` options**  

`./configure.sh --auto-download`

```

Call Stack (most recent call first):

  /usr/share/cmake/Modules/FindPython.cmake:580 (include)

title: Meaning of get-abduct
body:
I'm playing around with `get-abduct`. My understanding is that it's supposed to produce a predicate that is consistent with the assertions present, but contradicts when the given conjecture is added as well. So, I tried:

```
(set-logic QF_LIA)
(set-option :produce-abducts true)
(declare-fun x () Int)
(declare-fun y () Int)

(assert (>= x 0))
(get-abduct A (>= (+ x y) 2))
```

This prints:

```
(define-fun A () Bool (= y 2))
```

i.e., `y == 2` is claimed to be an abduct. Indeed, `x >= 0` and `y == 2` is consistent, but if I further conjunct with `x + y >= 2` (i.e., the conjecture), what we have is still satisfiable. That tells me `y == 2` isn't really an abduct. Am I reading this incorrectly?

title: Question about separation logic
body:
I apologize in advance if I am asking this question in the wrong place. In this case, feel encouraged to point out where this question should be asked.

I am new to CVC5 and separation logic, but I am slowly learning both of them. I did some simple queries and their results are very confusing to me. I asked the same [question](https://cs.stackexchange.com/questions/157764/what-is-the-difference-in-heap-configurations-separation-logic-with-cvc5-smt-so) on cs.stackexchange, but had no answer.

I will repeat my question here:

## First query

```
(set-logic QF_ALL)
(set-info :smt-lib-version 2.6)

(set-option :produce-models true)

; Heap declaration

(declare-heap (Int Int))

(declare-const v Int)

(assert (sep 
    (pto 1 v)
    (pto 2 v)
))

(check-sat)
(get-model)
```
### Result

```
sat
(
(define-fun v () Int 0)
)
(heap
(sep (pto 2 v) (pto 1 v))
(= (as sep.nil Int) 0)
)
```

## Second query

```
(set-logic QF_ALL)
(set-info :smt-lib-version 2.6)

(set-option :produce-models true)

; Heap declaration

(declare-heap (Int Int))

(declare-const v Int)

(assert (not (sep 
    (pto 1 v)
    (pto 2 v)
)))

(check-sat)
(get-model)
```

### Result

```
sat
(
(define-fun v () Int 0)
)
(heap
(sep (pto 2 0) (pto 1 0))
(= (as sep.nil Int) 0)
)
```

Why do both of these queries give SAT results? 

What is the difference between `pto 1 v` and `pto 1 0` while `v` equals zero?

What should I read to be able to understand these things myself?

title: Script fix-install-header.sh does not work properly on MacOS
body:
**Describe the bug**

The script `fix-install-header.sh` uses the 'sed' options `-i'' `, which do not work on Mac OS.
On Linux, this modifies `*.h` files in place. 

On MacOS, the syntax is `-i <extension>`  so this command creates a backup with suffix 'h-e' for every '.h' file.
Because the `find` applies sed to every file in the install `include` directory, the whole thing results in this:
```
> ls /usr/local/include/cvc5
cvc5.h                  cvc5_export.h           cvc5_kind.h             cvc5_sort_kind.h        cvc5_types.h
cvc5.h-e                cvc5_export.h-e         cvc5_kind.h-e           cvc5_sort_kind.h-e      cvc5_types.h-e
cvc5.h-e-e              cvc5_export.h-e-e       cvc5_kind.h-e-e         cvc5_sort_kind.h-e-e    cvc5_types.h-e-e
```

Things get worse if you install a new version as the sed command will create `.h-e-e-e-e-e` files and more every time.

This option is used for debugging the usefulness of theory lemmas.

Wasn't correct in the case of theory conflicts, which could lead to segfaults.

For this instance, cvc5 https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/commit/6a0abb70032db7bd747724477ca63372e7c801eb yields `sat` with `--bv-solver=bitblast-internal`, while yields `unsat` without the option.

On this example. cvc5 generates an invalid alethe proof. The proof contains an undeclared identifier `termITE_1`
```

invalid

title: Fix special cases for channel options
body:
Fixes #8900.

https://smtlib.cs.uiowa.edu/papers/smt-lib-reference-v2.6-r2021-05-12.pdf specifies that
`(set-option :regular-output-channel "stdout")`
should set the regular output channel to the standard out, whereas
`(set-option :regular-output-channel stdout)`
should result in a syntax error.

This would imply that our special cases are wrong in the option handlers for the channel options, which this PR corrects. 

Also note that:
`(set-option :regular-output-channel file.txt)`
would previously construct a file.txt, this is wrong, it should throw a syntax error, which it now does.
`(set-option :regular-output-channel "file.txt")`
will create the file `file.txt` now, whereas previously it incorrectly created `"file.txt"`.

title: Enable flex smt2 parser by default
body:
Includes several fixes found during testing:
- A check to avoid assertion failure in the flex parser
- Changes atomic SEXPR to symbols instead of constant strings to avoid spurious error messages for non-standard characters
- Changes to options configuration for Flex for performance (as a result, this does *not* fix  #9257).
- Fix for `--stdin-input-per-line` to not set incremental by default for non-interactive inputs.

Note that TPTP parsing still uses the ANTLR parser.

Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/issues/9258.
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/issues/8374.
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/issues/1862.
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/issues/791.
Fixes https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-wishues/issues/142.

title: Improvements to user-facing parser API
body:
This is in preparation for allowing the user to allocate parsers and parse terms from strings.

It makes it so that symbol manager is optional, moves the input parser to `parser/cpp/api` and simplifies a few things.

title: Make flex parser available via option
body:
This adds the option `--flex-parser`, which enables the flex parser. 

This option is pending performance testing, disabled at the moment.

Followup PRs will delete the ANTLR parser.

title: Adding a formula with declared constants in another solver object to sygus solver through the API
Pass optional output stream to computeType methods
body:
This is work towards eliminating exceptions from the type checker.

We now pass an (optional) output stream to getType, which will be used to output debugging information when type checking fails.

Follow-up PRs will make it so that type checking errors will: (1) return the null TypeNode, (2) write the error message to `errOut` if it exists.

title: Add option for eager reduction of positive membership into re concat
body:
The performance of industrial string benchmarks is sensitive to this option, although the overall impact is negative.

The option is disabled by default, thus, no behavior changes in this PR.

title: Ensure notifications for all options changes in set defaults
body:
This ensures that all changes to options in SetDefaults are notified in a uniform way.

The PR makes minor changes to defaults (e.g. the UF symmetry breaker is always auto-configured, but rarely is true, thus its default value is changed).  It also changes the logic slightly concerning when we notify when options changes.  We now notify whenever an option is changed (at verbosity=1), regardless of whether the change conflicts with a user option change.

This helps document the auto-configuration behavior of cvc5 for the user.

title: Segmentation Fault when Synthesizing Multiple Functions Given One Large Constraint
body:
Hi CVC5 team, We are working on synthesizing multiple functions with CVC5 given only one heavy constraint. If the constraint is relatively small, CVC5 synthesis succeeds. However, we found that if the constraint is large and complex beyond a certain point, CVC5 crashes when trying to synthesize exactly the same function signature. From what we can see, most crashes have to do with memory corruption.

After trying several queries for CVC5, we found most error messages for this issue to be as follows:

```shell
cvc5 suffered a segfault.
Offending address is 0x0
Looks like a NULL pointer was dereferenced.
zsh: segmentation fault
```

So we investigated these errors with the `-o sygus' option and found that CVC5 crashes when enumerating all terms and solution candidates. Our current suspicion is that there is a memory management issue in CVC5 that is causing this problem. We have attached an example of a relatively small SyGuS file that causes CVC5 to crash. This SyGuS file was generated by a higher-level synthesis tool we have developed. It is the smallest such file that we were able to construct that exhibited the crash.

**SyGuS File With Minimum Constraint Causing the Crash**

[axiom.sy](https://gist.github.com/ruchou/d938408c57f292d3b8321632dc903f77)

**cvc5 version**: 1.0.3 compiled with GCC version Apple LLVM 14.0.0 (clang-1400.0.29.202)

**Operating system**: macOS 13.1 (22C65)

We are currently encountering this crash on a significant number of the SyGuS files that are generated by our higher-level tool, so it is having a sizeable impact on our ability to use CVC5 for synthesis. Can you please take a look? If you need us to provide further information, don't hesitate to let us know. Thank you!

title: Avoid spurious equality engine trigger predicates
body:
Depends on https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/9443.

The purpose of this PR is to minimize redundant theory propagations.

This adds an option to check whether a literal is already asserted in the SAT solver when registering trigger predicates to the equality engine. In the case it is, it is not registered as a trigger predicate.

title: Add ieval failure with learning option to regressions
body: For the purposes of increasing code coverage, regressions chosen that exhibit non-trivial behavior in ieval.

title: [proofs] Adds option to optimize elaboration of macro resolution steps
body:
During post-processing we break each macro resolution steps into a series chain resolution + factoring steps. How many of these pairs we add is highfly influenced by how many "crowding literals" we have (i.e., literals that in the macro resolution have their duplicates implicitly deleted) and by how far down the chain they occur. This optimization is based on a heuristic to move these literals further down the chain when it is safe to do so.

In a challenge industrial benchmark this optimization leads to a 10x reduction in the expansion caused to the proof by the elaboration of macro resolution (2k added steps rather than 20k).

title: Add eager evaluation option for bv
body: This option is analogous to `--strings-eager-eval`, and allows us to turn off eager evaluation in equality engine.

title: Limiting the granularity of iand to be below 8
body: This is already enforced in `smt_options.cpp`, but now the check is moved to the options module.

title: Enable strings-exp by default
body:
This enables strings-exp whenever the logic includes strings, meaning the user should never have to worry about this option, unless they want to use `--no-strings-exp` as an optimization for string solving without extended functions / re memberships.

This required fixing a bug in the quantifiers bound inference module that incorrectly set bounds for variables when strings-exp was enabled.

title: Branch on option string names using hash map and switch-case
Cache option values in command executor
body:
This avoids calling Solver::getOptionInfo on each command invocation, which is currently a fairly expensive method.

This PR helps 30% or more on parsing time for large benchmarks in my initial testing, prior to making getOptionInfo more efficient.

title: [proofs] [alethe] Use let binder in Alethe printer
body: Have the Alethe printer optionally both compute and apply sharing via Alethe's let binding.

title: Fix check-unsat-cores and minimal-unsat-cores
body:
This fixes bugs related to checking unsat cores and minimal unsat cores.

Both features applied top-level substitutions to assertions-to-check, which includes definitions for define-fun and substitutions learned via non-clausal simplification.  This may lead to incorrectly determining that an unsat core is unsatisfiable.

This meant that
(1) `--minimal-unsat-cores` could produce incorrect unsat cores
(2) `--check-unsat-cores` could fail to realize when an unsat core was incorrect.

The PR ensures that top-level substitutions are not applied, and assertions corresponding to definitions are treated via `defineFunction` instead of `assertFormula` on the subsolver.

This furthermore corrects an issue with unsat cores + `--macro-quant` where we were producing incorrect unsat cores but failing to realize it.  It also disables unsat cores from 2 regressions where `--check-unsat-cores` now times out.

A minimized regression for minimal-unsat-cores is added.

This may make these options slightly slower, since non-trivial substitutions must be rederived the subsolver.

title: Bad performance on large problems with check-sat-assuming commands
body:
Hello,

I noticed that cvc5 performs significantly worse compared to other SMT solvers when solving large QF_LIA problems with multiple `check-sat-assuming` commands. Here are a couple of examples: [examples.zip](https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/files/10059574/examples.zip)

z3 and Yices 2 solve the whole script `DRAGON_4_e2_2799.lus.ic3.1.smt2` in 2s on my laptop; MathSAT in 7s. In constrast, cvc5 takes 55s. Runtime goes down to 38s if I use cvc5 option `--ext-rew-prep=use`.

The time differece is even more significant when solving the other example (`FIREFLY_7.lus.ic3.1.smt2`). Here are the runtimes on my laptop: z3: 5s, Yices 2: 5s; MathSAT: 21s; cvc5 (default options): 3m45s; cvc5 (with `--ext-rew-prep=use`): 3m11s

**Command line arguments**: `--incremental` and `--ext-rew-prep=use`
**cvc5 version/commit**:  cvc5-Linux-2022-11-19-4ae9c2c
**Operating system**: Ubuntu 20.04

title: Do not get the input language via getOption in the parser
body:
https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/7074 introduced noticeable performance issues in our parser where `Solver::getOption` could be the bottleneck on large input files, especially with string literals.

https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/pull/8592 eliminated our calls to getOption when parsing string literals.

This PR eliminates the remaining calls to `Solver::getOption("input-language")` from the parser.

It also corrects an unintentional inconsistency where string literals would use ad-hoc escape sequences when we were parsing sygus.

title: Do not report infeasible for smart enumeration + any-constant constructors
body:
We currently (intentionally) overprune any-constant constructor model values, by not considering the concrete model value of their arguments when using smart enumeration in SyGuS solver.  This incompleteness was not accounted for yet, hence we could return `infeasible` incorrectly for grammars that had finitely many values modulo any-constant argument values.  https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5-projects/issues/222 was an example.

This also corrects a bug where the SyGuS conjecture itself was being included in the assertions to check with `--check-synth-sol`, making the option less trustworthy and was causing checks to fail due to the change on this PR.

title: Parse S-expressions as terms
body:
Fixes #8900. Currently,

```
(set-option :diagnostic-output-channel "stdout")
```

creates a `"stdout"` file, because the parser parses all S-expressions
(except nested ones) as strings. However, for values used in
`set-option` commands, this causes a problem because string values are
stored including the double quotes, which throws off our option handlers
that do not expect those double quotes. However, we cannot simply remove
the double quotes for strings in S-expressions, because otherwise some
S-expressions are printed incorrectly (e.g., `(set-info :foo "bar bar")`
would be printed as `(set-info :foo bar bar)`, which is incorrect).

This commit implements a solution that refactors the parser to parse
S-expressions as terms. For the `set-option` command, the commit removes
the double quotes around strings. As a result, `-o raw-benchmark` may
dump `set-option` commands with the double quotes removed, which is not
perfect, but could be fixed by further refactoring `SetOptionCommand` to
store a `Term` instead of an `std::string` for the value.

This change allows us to share some code for parsing "special constants"
in terms and S-expressions as defined in the SMT-LIB standard. The
commit also fixes a minor issue where whitespace characters were
expected to be escaped, which is incorrect according to the SMT-LIB
standard (the previous code called an ad-hoc string escape routing that
handled these cases before the string was stored in a
`cvc5::internal::String`). Finally, the change requires us to be careful
when generating strings from S-expressions: real values must be printed
as decimal numbers and not fractions.

title: Error: incomparable types in match case list
body:
Confusing error ` incomparable types in match case list` for simple case:

```
(set-logic AUFDTLIA)

(declare-datatypes ((Maybe 1))
  ((par (T) ((Nothing)
             (Just (value T))))))

(define-fun f ((optional (Maybe Int))) (Maybe Int)
  (match optional
    ((Nothing Nothing)
     ((Just value) (Just value)))))

(declare-const c1 (Maybe Int))
(assert (= c1 (f (Just 1))))

(check-sat)
```

Workaround: replace `Nothing` term to `(as Nothing (Maybe Int))`:

(define-fun f ((optional (Maybe Int))) (Maybe Int)

title: Remove superfluous 'lbsd' for Editline
body:
On some systems (e.g., openSUSE), you can link against `editline` *without* having the BSD compatibility libraries. For example, on my machine, I have `libedit-devel` installed without having `libbsd-devel`, which then leads to:

```
: && /usr/bin/c++ -fPIC -fno-inline -Og -Wall -Wsuggest-override -Wnon-virtual-dtor -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Wshadow -fno-extern-tls-init -Wno-class-memaccess -ggdb3 -g -flto -fno-fat-lto-objects   -shared -Wl,-soname,libmain-test.so -o src/main/libmain-test.so src/main/CMakeFiles/main.dir/command_executor.cpp.o src/main/CMakeFiles/main.dir/interactive_shell.cpp.o src/main/CMakeFiles/main.dir/signal_handlers.cpp.o src/main/CMakeFiles/main.dir/time_limit.cpp.o src/main/CMakeFiles/main.dir/options.cpp.o src/main/CMakeFiles/main-test.dir/driver_unified.cpp.o  -Wl,-rpath,/home/avj/clones/cvc5/master/build/src/parser:/home/avj/clones/cvc5/master/build/src:/home/avj/clones/cvc5/master/build/deps/lib64:/home/avj/clones/cvc5/master/build/deps/lib  src/parser/libcvc5parser.so.1  -ledit  -lbsd  -ltinfo  src/libcvc5.so  deps/lib64/libcln.so  deps/lib/libpolyxx.so  deps/lib/libpoly.so  /usr/lib64/libgmp.so && :
/usr/lib64/gcc/x86_64-suse-linux/11/../../../../x86_64-suse-linux/bin/ld: cannot find -lbsd
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

However, there is no requirement that you need `lbsd` when linking `ledit`.

This PR therefore makes it such that `bsd` is only linked when you're using `editline` if you have it.

Signed-off-by: Andrew V. Teylu <andrew@tey.lu>

title: Migrating GLPK patches from 4.52 to 5.0
body:
# Overview

This PR updates the integration of `cvc5` with GLPK from version 4.52 (released: 2013-07-18) to version 5.0 (released: 2020-12-16).

Some important notes about the transition from 4.52 to 5.0:

* Releases of GLPK from (at least) 4.52 through to 4.65 (the last release in the 4.x series) contained code that was **not licensed for commercial use** (_"[t]his routine is in the public domain to be used only for research purposes. It cannot be used as part of a commercial product, or to satisfy in any part commercial delivery requirements to government or industry"_) -- see: https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/info-gnu/2020-12/msg00007.html and https://github.com/timothy-king/glpk-cut-log/blob/b420454e732f4b3d229c552ef7cd46fec75fe65c/src/misc/relax4.c#L139

* The files `glpspx01.c` (removed in 4.56) and `glpspx02.c` (removed in 4.57) implementing the "primal simplex method" and the "dual simplex method" were removed from GLPK; they have been replaced with a _"more efficient and robust implementation of the primal simplex method"_ (4.56) and a _"more efficient implementation of the dual simplex method"_ (4.57); more on this later

* A number of files from 4.52 have been split into multiple files by the time that 5.0 was released; for example, `glpios05.c` has been split into `gmicut.c` and `gmigen.c`


# Changes in this branch

I've followed the GLPK ChangeLog between 4.52 to 5.0 to try to work-out where files have moved/renamed/split, as well as tracking down where functionality has been moved/renamed (e.g., via refactoring, etc.).

Where code has been "totally removed" from GLPK (e.g., in the case of `glpspx01.c`/`glpspx02.c`, I have commented these sections out in the GLPK patches, such that this content isn't lost. Also, to aid in review effort, I've manually reordered the content in the patch to match the file order as-per the current head.

For the most part, I feel I've managed to forward-port the patches from 2013 to the 2020 release, without any loss of behaviour between what exists in both 4.52 and 5.0.

## Things I haven't done

As highlighted above, GLPK 4.56/4.57 removed the old simplex implementations in favour of more efficient ones -- I **have not** attempts to forward-port Tim's changes into this the new simplex solver yet. This means that the content inside of 5.0's `src/simplex/` folder does not yet have the logic for terminating early when there are "stability failures". It does not seem that the old simplex implementation logged when there were cuts (at least not in the files that were removed), so I am hoping this is a low-risk change.


# Assessing performance

As `--use-approx` is a mode that is enabled in `cvc5` in "competitive mode", it would clearly be disadvantageous if the migration to GLPK 5.0 had a performance impact. Given limited resources, I have attempted to compare master (@ d72b82ba383cb1e0cccab33218fdf5af280ec7cb) *without GLPK*, master *with 4.52* (same hash) and this PR *with 5.0* (only one commit on top of d72b82ba383cb1e0cccab33218fdf5af280ec7cb), but limited to a timeout of *1 minute*.

I ran each benchmark 5 times (for each configuration) on a "Intel Xeon Gold 6258R" @ 2.70GHz, with the same options (that is, master was called with `--use-approx` even though it was not a GLPK build), on the whole of QF_LIA, QF_LIA-inc, QF_LRA and QF_LRA-inc. In what follows, I only consider those benchmarks for which master timed-out on *every* execution and 4.52 *did not* time-out even once.

## High-level stats

* Total files assessed: 165

* Files timing-out within 1 minute *without GLPK*: 165

* Files timing-out within 1 minute *with 4.52*: 0

* Files timing-out within 1 minute *with 5.0*: 6

* Files *not* timing-out with 5.0: 159

* Sum of average time for 4.52 on those 159: 417.89s

* Sum of average time for 5.0 on those 159: 333.21s

This shows that, when 5.0 finishes within the timeout, it is quicker (on average), but there are six benchmarks where it is slower. These are:

*  `./QF_LIA/20180326-Bromberger/more_slacked/CAV_2009_benchmarks/coef-size/smt/size-100/c100_problem__005.smt2.slack.smt2`
* `./QF_LIA/20180326-Bromberger/more_slacked/CAV_2009_benchmarks/coef-size/smt/size-30/c30_problem__005.smt2.slack.smt2`
* `./QF_LIA/20180326-Bromberger/more_slacked/CAV_2009_benchmarks/coef-size/smt/size-40/c40_problem__003.smt2.slack.smt2`
* `./QF_LIA/20180326-Bromberger/more_slacked/CAV_2009_benchmarks/smt/30-vars/v30_problem__034.smt2.slack.smt2`
* `./QF_LIA/20180326-Bromberger/more_slacked/cut_lemmas/15-vars/cut_lemma_03_011.smt2.slack.smt2`
* `./QF_LIA/20180326-Bromberger/unbd-sage/unbd050v55c/unbd-sage14.smt2`

## Detailed stats

The following is a breakdown of running 5.0 across the 165 files that *never* timed-out with 4.52 but *always* timed-out on a build without GLPK.

Columns are as follows:

title: Is `ApproxNoOp` "dead code" and therefore should be removed?
body:
In discussing #6958, @4tXJ7f pointed out that that the `--use-approx` code only is triggered if we have `options::useApprox()` and `ApproximateSimplex::enabled()`:

- https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/blob/e4e19cd62b3eebed2de5b9b627509df0ffec23e1/src/theory/arith/theory_arith_private.cpp#L1884-L1885
- https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/blob/e4e19cd62b3eebed2de5b9b627509df0ffec23e1/src/theory/arith/theory_arith_private.cpp#L2969

If this is the case, then it means that [`ApproximateSimplex::mkApproximateSimplexSolver`](https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/blob/bd33d20609999f6f847aeb63a42350aeb3041406/src/theory/arith/approx_simplex.cpp#L538) is only called if we have GLPK.

If `ApproximateSimplex::mkApproximateSimplexSolver` is only called only GLPK-enabled builds, then this means that `return new ApproxNoOp(vars, l, s);` is never invoked:

- https://github.com/cvc5/cvc5/blob/bd33d20609999f6f847aeb63a42350aeb3041406/src/theory/arith/approx_simplex.cpp#L539-L543

and therefore the whole of `ApproxNoOp` is never actually used in `cvc5`.

Does this mean that this is a candidate for removal? If so, I'm happy to put this in a PR and clean-up  `ApproximateSimplex::mkApproximateSimplexSolver` -- I guess we need to decide what it should do if someone mistakenly calls it in non-GLPK builds (assert? return NULL?).

title: Assertion failure when mixing arrays and floating-point
body:
cvc4 gives an assertion failure on an input that uses both arrays and floating-point.

```
$ cat delta.out.smt2 
(declare-fun fpv () (_ FloatingPoint 8 24))
(declare-fun afp () (Array (_ FloatingPoint 8 24) (_ FloatingPoint 8 24)))
(assert (= fpv (select afp (fp.neg fpv))))
(check-sat)

$ bin/cvc4 delta.out.smt2 
Fatal failure within CVC4::Node CVC4::theory::fp::FpConverter::getValue(CVC4::theory::Valuation&, CVC4::TNode) at /home/gereon/cvc4/src/theory/fp/fp_converter.cpp:1708
Check failure

 Theory::isLeafOf(var, THEORY_FP)

Aborted (core dumped)
```

**Command line arguments**: none
**CVC4 version/commit**: 21439d98e9afe1541bb0f5371c4ab0011666bd5e

title: CLN runtime error in nonlinear extension with --ubsan
body:
**Describe the bug**
I observe the following output
`/usr/include/cln/object.h:121:16: runtime error: left shift of negative value -1`
on this smt2 file

    (set-logic QF_NRA)
    (declare-fun x () Real)
    (assert (= (* x x) 2))
    (assert (< (+ x (* x x)) 3))
    (check-sat)

I traced it to [arith_msum.cpp:183](https://github.com/CVC4/CVC4/blob/master/src/theory/arith/arith_msum.cpp#L183). Adding the following lines immediately before the if

    Trace("nl-ext") << "Before: " << cln::numerator(r.getValue()) << " / " << cln::denominator(r.getValue()) << std::endl;
    r.isNegativeOne();
    Trace("nl-ext") << "After" << std::endl;

produces this output (with `-t nl-ext`):

    Before: -1 / 1
    /usr/include/cln/object.h:121:16: runtime error: left shift of negative value -1
    After

Interestingly, the error only happens once, though CVC4 does not bail out but seems to continue the computation just fine.

**Command line arguments**: Command line arguments passed to CVC4 if applicable
**CVC4 version/commit**: Current master, 5938faaf034a761f3462d8e03b86b1726a332f68
**Operating system**: Ubuntu 20.04 with libcln-dev 1.3.6-4build1

**`configure.sh` options**
`./configure.sh --cln --ubsan --tracing --gpl`

The issue vanishes when `--ubsan` is not used.

title: SMT2 parser accepts quote char (') from file but not from stdin
body:
```
$ cat print.smt2
(set-option :incremental false)
(set-info :source "ABC
ABC'00
http://www.xx.x.x.x/x/")
$ cat print.smt2 | builds/bin/cvc4 --lang=smt2
(error "Parse Error: <stdin>:3.23: Extended/unprintable characters are not part of SMT-LIB, and they must be encoded as escape sequences")
$ builds/bin/cvc4 --lang=smt2 print.smt2
$
```

Note: The issue might be a bit more complicated than it seems because changing the non-quote chars in the string can change the error message to:

```
$ cat print.smt2
(set-option :incremental false)
(set-info :source "ABC
ABC'00
http://www.x.x.x/x/")
$ cat print.smt2 | builds/bin/cvc4 --lang=smt2
(error "Parse Error: <stdin>:3.20: basic_string::_M_create")
```
